title: Quitting Cab Calloway over a humiliation
summary: After exhausting theater runs and Cab's rehearsal demands, an incident leads him to give notice and leave without his fare.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So they start getting on my nerves the guys in the (inaudible). So one day -- we'd been traveling now for 20 -- we'd been doing 20 week of theaters. We used to do a whole lot of theater. You know, 20 week of theater would run anybody crazy. We used to do five, four, five shows a day.

And Cab was a funny guy at the time too. But the band begin to get on his nerves too, because like he feel that the band was too big for him and that he didn't know enough, he didn't know enough music to compete with (inaudible). So he used to call REHEARSAL 6:00 o'clock in the morning, could you score this stuff. (Inaudible) do this hear, you know, trying to impress people, you know.

So is to talk bad to some of those guys, you know what I mean. I used to say, oh, I hope this man never (inaudible). I hope. We are good friend, and I don't, you know, you never can tell. So we were working, and I think we were up around -- somewhere around Detroit or somewhere around there, the theater.

We had in the show a lady by name of Avis Andrews, beautiful singer, had some beautiful arrangements, you know. And some of the effects used to play in the Derby. If you play in the Derby, you got to be careful. If you put home too much
(inaudible) some notes, you be out of tune, because (inaudible). So he ran (inaudible), he say, get your (inaudible). I got to hear the sound right.

So he uses one (inaudible), say, you (inaudible). So right after the show I came to the dressing room. He say -- I said, Cab, I hate to tell you this, man, but what I didn't want to happen just happened today. And this, the first time I (inaudible) the last time I go (inaudible). So you take my notice? Oh, yeah, I take your notice. Okay.

Same thing happened. Everybody here said, man, you crazy. Where you going, man? You leave the best job. I said, I don't care. I want a band with dignity. That's all. Say, look, I know how to work. I'm a musician. I know how music is supposed to be played. I don't have to take something like that. (Inaudible). Well, don't worry about it. Well, all right.

So the day I'm supposed to close at Buffalo, I think (inaudible) New England. Cab, you know today my last day? And I want to say goodbye, and I want to get my fare back home. He said, no, I won't pay you no fare home. You pay your own fare home. You quit. And if I -- I don't want you to go, but you want to go.
All right. I left. So every (inaudible), every time they come to town, they come to me. So I already had in my mind
